pages.text: Dad the fisherman poured steaming water into the yard tub. "Is it still hot?" Riri in her yellow hat dipped just her toes, then pulled them out. The summer evening yard smelled of warm water.
"I must wash before the lighthouse lights up!" Riri dipped her toes again. "A little later. It is hot now." Lolo in yellow boots had finished washing and wore a towel over their shoulders.
As she kept dipping and withdrawing, the steam disappeared. The water grew lukewarm. Riri's arms were still sticky, with gritty sand on her back.
Dad put his hand in and stirred. Water rolled in and out. "Riri, there are waves in the tub too!"
Riri peered into the tub. Little waves rolled back and forth. "One when a wave comes in, two when it goes out." Dad pushed the water. "On three, get in up to your shoulders."
Riri took a deep breath. A wave came in. "One." It went out. "Two." It came in again. "Three!"
Riri slipped into the tub up to her shoulders. Warm water lapped at her neck. "Now I am in, it is not hot at all!" Waves in the tub—splash!
Sand washed gently off Riri's back. Dad trickled water over her head with a dipper. Lolo splashed into the overflow with those boots.
The next evening, Riri reached the tub first. "Count three waves and slip in! Water trickles over my head! It laps at my shoulders!" She hung her hat on the rim and lifted a leg over.
Dad wrapped Riri in a towel and hugged her. Keep testing too long, and the water cools. Count just three, and you can slip in. "Waves in the tub—splash!" Riri smiled inside the towel.
